newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe launches economic consultative forum.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe launches economic consultative forum.

text.p: Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe launched a National Economic Consultative Forum on Wednesday aimed at improving cooperation between the government, the private sector and labour in policy formulation.

Speaking at the launch, Mugabe said he hoped the forum -- made up of 62 members and chaired by Industry and Commerce Minister Nathan Shamuyarira -- would help mobilise investment and also to speed up some long-standing government programmes.

"I would like to emphasise that the planned targets should be aimed at those areas that are catalytical to overall economic growth such as mobilisation of financial resources for the medium and long-term investment, acceleration of commercialisation and privatisation of state enterprises," he said.

Mugabe also called on the forum to recommend strategies that could be employed to promote participation of Zimbabwe's black majority people in an economy in which the state, multinational corporations and minority whites dominate.
The government say black economic empowerment -- called indigenisation -- is now a key component of its economic policies because it was necessary for political stability.
On Wednesday Mugabe appealed for all-round support, saying there was a role for private business, unions and the government.
He said big corporations could allow workers to have shares in some of those multinationals employing them.
